title: Deliverables exist and initiative_portfolio.json carries the required structure
check_description: Verifies both deliverables were submitted and initiative_portfolio.json has the required shape: baseline, 5-10 initiatives each carrying the required fields, a sequencing list, and >=3 risks.
score_1_criteria: demand_growth_plan.md and initiative_portfolio.json both exist; initiatives list has 5-10 entries; every initiative carries non-empty initiative_id, name, segment, thesis, revenue_impact_band_usd_m, cost_to_execute_band_usd_k, timeline_quarters, evidence_sources; sequencing has >=3 entries; risks has >=3 entries.
score_0_criteria: Any of: a deliverable missing; fewer than 5 or more than 10 initiatives; any initiative missing a required field or leaving it empty; sequencing fewer than 3 entries; risks fewer than 3 entries.
specific_file_locations: Structure is defined in tasks/t1.md (deliverable schema paragraph); no source files required for this structural gate.

title: Baseline fidelity: revenue, blended margin, active accounts, segment coverage
check_description: Verifies the structured baseline reproduces the source-anchored FY2025 baseline: revenue $481.2M, blended GM 19.8%, 2,614 active accounts, and at least 5 segments.
score_1_criteria: baseline.revenue_usd_m in [479, 483.5]; baseline.gross_margin_pct in [19.5, 20.1] (or fraction equivalent 0.195-0.201); baseline.active_accounts in [2550, 2680]; baseline.segments has >=5 entries.
score_0_criteria: Any baseline figure outside its band (notably: using the 3,100/3,109 account count; a blended margin computed without the dormant-account or mix corrections; revenue materially off $481.2M), or fewer than 5 segments.
specific_file_locations: financials_by_segment_fy23_fy25.csv FY2025 rows sum to 481.2 revenue / 95.2 GP (19.8% blended); margin_waterfall_fy2325.csv 'FY2025 blended GM, 19.8'; crm_data_dictionary.md: '3,109 account records: 2,614 active, 495 dormant'.

title: Portfolio covers the load-bearing initiative areas
check_description: Verifies the initiative portfolio addresses the four load-bearing demand levers the sources support: street/independent demand, healthcare whitespace, private label, and digital ordering including the compensation barrier.
score_1_criteria: Initiatives include at least one targeting the street segment and one targeting healthcare (segment fields), and the portfolio text covers private label, the portal/digital-ordering push, and the commission/comp-plan redesign.
score_0_criteria: Any load-bearing area absent — e.g., a digital initiative with no mention of commissions/comp plan (ignoring comp_plan_2025.md section 4.3 and the rep-fear evidence), or no healthcare initiative despite the Heartland material.
specific_file_locations: comp_plan_2025.md section 4.3: 'Orders placed through the Bluestem Direct portal are processed under house-account administration.'; gpo_postmortem.eml: 98.5% fill-rate requirement and spring 2027 rebid; private_label_line_card.md: 9.0% penetration, +620 bps.
v1_change: E5-D07: the comp-plan leg's bare token 'incentive' passed any portfolio mentioning e.g. 'volume incentive rebates'; replaced by sales-compensation phrases (commission, comp plan, compensation, sales/rep incentive, incentive plan/pay/comp).

title: Street digital uplift sized from triangulated sources
check_description: Verifies the digital-ordering opportunity is sized inside the triangulation band ($4.2-6.9M incremental street revenue), which requires joining the CRM adoption count, the portal order-size delta, and street revenue per account.
score_1_criteria: demand_growth_plan.md states a digital/e-commerce uplift figure in $4.2M-$6.9M on a digital-context line (the triangulated sizing).
score_0_criteria: No quantified digital uplift; or a figure far outside the band (e.g., sized off Dale's 'over half' adoption claim, off the national 65% benchmark applied as immediate adoption, or off order counts instead of account revenue).
specific_file_locations: crm_data_dictionary.md: '492 of 1,588 active street accounts (31.0%)'; portal_order_analytics_fy2025.csv FY rows: portal avg $1,563 vs rep $1,434 (+9.0%); financials CSV FY2025 street row: 212.6 revenue / 1,588 accounts = $133.9K.

title: Price-cut thesis refuted; no across-the-board price cut recommended (trap)
check_description: Verifies the plan does NOT adopt the VP Sales across-the-board price-reduction thesis, and engages the Springfield pilot evidence (+1.8% volume for -8.8% GP dollars, implied elasticity ~-0.7). Machine core: no initiative NAME proposes a price cut (naming the rejected thesis in a thesis/risk field to reject it is fine and expected), and the pilot is engaged quantitatively via ANY of the volume response (~1.8%), the implied elasticity (~0.7), or the GP impact (~8.8%). Whether the PROSE recommends the cut is judged manually from the recommendation itself.
score_1_criteria: No initiative is named as a broad price cut, AND the plan cites the pilot's volume response (~1.8%), implied elasticity (~-0.7), or GP decline (~8.8%) when rejecting the thesis. Targeted, surgical price actions (e.g., fixing below-minimum drops) under names like 'pricing hygiene' are acceptable.
score_0_criteria: The plan recommends an across-the-board or broad street price reduction (Dale's 4-6% proposal), or rejects the thesis without engaging the pilot data at all.
specific_file_locations: price_pilot_analysis_fy2024.csv: pilot vs control rows aggregating to -2.6% realized price, +1.8% cases, -8.8% GP dollars; vp_sales_growth_memo.md: the 4-6% across-the-board proposal and 'volume responded immediately'; customer_survey_results.csv: price rank 4, weighted score 6.8.
v1_change: E5-D08/E5-D09: non-vacuity gate on initiatives; trap names broadened ('price reset', 'across-the-board', 'price decrease', 'blanket price', 'price rollback'). The elasticity leg now reads '-0.7' as 0.7 (no sign parsing in v1).

title: House style: banned phrases absent, FY format and bps convention used
check_description: Verifies the prose deliverable obeys the H&V engagement standards: no banned phrases (synergy, world-class, best-in-class), fiscal years written FY20xx, and margin changes expressed in bps.
score_1_criteria: demand_growth_plan.md contains none of the banned phrases; uses the FY20xx format at least 3 times; and expresses at least one margin change in 'bps'.
score_0_criteria: Any banned phrase appears; or fiscal-year convention ignored; or no margin change stated in bps anywhere.
specific_file_locations: harrow_vance_engagement_standards.md: rules list — banned phrases 'synergy'/'synergies', 'world-class', 'best-in-class'; 'Fiscal years are written as FY2025'; 'margin CHANGES are stated in basis points (bps)'.
v1_change: E5-D05/E5-D10: unscoped ban kept (source-backed writing standard); flagged house_style_ban.

title: Initiatives carry document-name evidence sourcing
check_description: Verifies every initiative lists evidence_sources and that the portfolio cites real quantitative source documents (per the H&V attribution standard).
score_1_criteria: Every initiative has a non-empty evidence_sources list, and the cited names include at least one of the core quantitative sources (financials_by_segment_fy23_fy25.csv, mdc_benchmark_study_2025.md, delivery_cost_study_fy2025.csv).
score_0_criteria: Any initiative lacks evidence_sources; or citations are invented/generic ('internal data') with none of the real quantitative source documents named anywhere in the portfolio.
specific_file_locations: harrow_vance_engagement_standards.md: 'Every quantified initiative must name the client source document(s) supporting its sizing.'
v1_change: E5-D07: required source names matched without the file extension (a bare 'csv' no longer covers 'financials_by_segment_fy23_fy25.csv'; the v1 enum is one-directional).

title: Mix-shift trap diagnosed quantitatively in the prose
check_description: Verifies the prose plan quantifies the central diagnosis: ~$29M of revenue growth FY2023-FY2025 produced ~$0.5M of gross-profit growth as blended GM compressed from 20.9% to 19.8%.
score_1_criteria: demand_growth_plan.md states the FY2023-FY2025 revenue growth (~$29.1M, accept 28.5-29.7), the gross-profit stall (~$0.5M, accept 0.2-1.0), and the FY2023 blended margin (~20.9%, accept 20.7-21.1) or equivalently the ~110 bps compression.
score_0_criteria: The mix-shift diagnosis is missing, purely qualitative, or uses wrong figures (e.g., treats chain gross margin growth as profit growth, or reports GP growth materially above $1M).
specific_file_locations: financials CSV: FY2023 sum 452.1/94.7 vs FY2025 481.2/95.2; margin_waterfall_fy2325.csv: 20.9 -> 19.8 with -65 bps mix / -46 bps rate; CFO transcript: 'twenty-nine million of new revenue and about half a million dollars of new gross profit'.

title: Marketing measurement addressed, not swallowed
check_description: Verifies the plan addresses the food-show/marketing ROI gap: cites the $410K show cost and treats attribution as broken rather than accepting the $3.2M pipeline claim.
score_1_criteria: The plan mentions the food show / marketing attribution problem (at least two of: food show, attribution, campaign_source, marketing ROI, lead tracking) and cites the $410K show cost; if the $3.2M figure appears it is framed as unverified/self-reported, not as demand evidence.
score_0_criteria: Marketing measurement ignored entirely; or the $3.2M pipeline treated as validated demand; or an expanded food-show initiative sized on untracked pipeline.
specific_file_locations: food_show_recap_2026.md: '$3.2M in qualified pipeline', $410K cost; email_thread_marketing_roi.eml (Ellery): 'campaign_source was populated on 6.3% of post-show orders. Orders we can actually attribute to the April show total $241K.'

title: Sequencing respects cash, capacity, and dependency logic
check_description: Human-judged: verifies the sequencing is internally coherent — the comp-plan redesign precedes or accompanies the portal push (not after it); KC-metro volume initiatives are gated on the Q2 2027 racking project or routed to Tulsa/Springfield; the healthcare fill-rate investment lands before the spring 2027 Heartland rebid; and phased spend stays within ~$6M/yr capex plus revolver headroom.
score_1_criteria: All four sequencing logics hold: comp redesign not sequenced after the portal push it enables; KC capacity constraint respected; fill-rate investment scheduled ahead of spring 2027; total phased cost consistent with the stated capital constraints.
score_0_criteria: Any inversion: portal push scheduled before/without the comp fix; KC-metro volume growth assumed before capacity exists; healthcare initiative timed after the rebid; or aggregate near-term spend that ignores the $6M capex / covenant envelope.
specific_file_locations: ops_constraints_memo.md: KC 91% cube until Q2 2027 racking ($2.1M); $1.4M fill-rate package; comp_plan_2025.md section 4.3 (house-rate portal coding); gpo_postmortem.eml: 'rebid lands spring 2027'; ceo letter: ~$6M capex, $25M revolver.

title: Churn definitions reconciled; 8.5% net revenue attrition used for planning
check_description: Cross-source consistency: verifies the plan reconciles the 19% CRM lapse figure against finance's 8.5% net revenue attrition and uses the controller's authoritative definition, with the seasonal/90-day-lapse mechanism explained.
score_1_criteria: claims.json key_figures.net_revenue_attrition_pct in [8.0, 9.0]; the prose uses ~8.5% as the planning figure near churn/attrition/retention language and explains the 90-day-lapse or seasonal K-12 mechanism behind the inflated 19% figure.
score_0_criteria: The plan uses 19% (or ~19.3%) as the churn planning figure; or reports 8.5% without any reconciliation; or claims.json figure outside [8.0, 9.0].
specific_file_locations: controller_churn_reconciliation_memo.md: 19.3% lapse -> 11.2% account attrition -> 8.5% net revenue attrition; 'The 19% figure should not appear in planning documents'; vp_sales_growth_memo.md: 'churn running at 19%'; crm_data_dictionary.md: lapse_90d_flag is 'a re-engagement trigger, not an attrition metric'.

title: Chain contribution margin computed near zero; growth-engine claim refuted
check_description: Cross-source consistency: verifies the plan joins segment gross margin (12.2%) with delivery cost-to-serve (11.3%) to show chain contribution margin of ~0.9%, refuting the VP Sales 'profitable growth engine' claim.
score_1_criteria: claims.json key_figures.chain_contribution_margin_pct in [0.3, 1.6]; the prose states a chain contribution figure in that band near contribution/margin language; the diagnosis rejects chasing chain volume as the demand answer.
score_0_criteria: Chain profitability assessed at the gross-margin line only (~12%); or the delivery cost allocation ignored; or claims.json figure outside [0.3, 1.6]; or the plan endorses chain growth as the primary profitable demand lever.
specific_file_locations: financials CSV FY2025 chains row: 128.4 / 12.2%; delivery_cost_study_fy2025.csv chains FY total: 41,600 drops x $349 = $14,518K (11.3% of revenue); CFO transcript: 'less than a point of contribution margin'; VP memo: 'profitable growth' claim.

title: Private-label gap sized against the correct peer cohort (18-22%), not the 10% trap
check_description: Cross-source consistency: verifies the plan benchmarks Bluestem's 9.0% PL penetration against the MDC regional-broadline cohort (median 19.6%, IQR 18-22%) rather than the junior analyst's 10% figure pulled from the convenience-channel row.
score_1_criteria: claims.json key_figures.private_label_penetration_pct in [8.5, 9.5]; the prose cites a peer benchmark in the 18-22% range (accept 17.5-22.5) near private-label/benchmark language; the PL initiative is sized as a material upside, not dismissed as 'at market'.
score_0_criteria: The plan uses ~10% as the peer benchmark (Tyler's wrong cohort row) or concludes PL is 'at market'; or the claims.json penetration figure outside [8.5, 9.5]; or no peer benchmark cited at all.
specific_file_locations: private_label_line_card.md: $43.3M = 9.0%, +620 bps premium; mdc_benchmark_study_2025.md Exhibit 4: regional broadline median 19.6% (IQR 18-22); convenience-channel row 10.4% (the trap); slack 2026-05-12 Tyler: 'peer private label penetration is like 10%'.

title: Active-account discrepancy resolved via the data dictionary
check_description: Cross-source consistency: verifies the plan uses the ~2,614 active-account base and resolves the 3,100-vs-2,600 conflict via the dormant-account definition rather than averaging or picking arbitrarily.
score_1_criteria: The prose uses an active-account figure in [2550, 2680] and explains the dormant-record distinction (495 dormant / no order in trailing 365 days) behind the 3,100 figure.
score_0_criteria: The plan uses ~3,100 as the account base; or presents both numbers without resolution; or sizes per-account initiatives off the inflated base.
specific_file_locations: crm_data_dictionary.md: '3,109 account records: 2,614 active, 495 dormant' with the 365-day active definition; food_show_recap_2026.md: 'more than 3,100 customers'; ceo letter: 'roughly 2,600 active accounts'.

title: Digital adoption stated at 31% against the 65% peer median
check_description: Cross-source consistency: verifies the plan quantifies street portal adoption at ~31% (CRM field count) against the MDC peer median of 65% (top quartile 74%), rejecting the VP Sales 'over half' claim.
score_1_criteria: The prose states street digital adoption in [29, 33]% near portal/digital language AND a peer benchmark in [60, 75]% near peer/benchmark language.
score_0_criteria: Adoption stated per Dale's 'over half'; or no current-adoption figure; or the gap framed without the peer benchmark; or order-share (20%) conflated with account adoption without explanation.
specific_file_locations: crm_data_dictionary.md: 'portal_enrolled = Y on 492 of 1,588 active street accounts (31.0%)'; mdc_benchmark_study_2025.md Exhibit 7: median 65%, top quartile 74%; slack 2026-05-19 Dale: 'over half our street customers are already ordering online anyway'.

title: Heartland GPO loss attributed to service levels; fill-rate gap quantified
check_description: Cross-source consistency: verifies the healthcare initiative is grounded in the customer's own debrief — lost on a 98.5% fill-rate SLA vs Bluestem's 94.1%, pricing within 1.5% — not on the VP Sales 'lost on price' narrative.
score_1_criteria: The prose names Heartland, states the required ~98.5% fill rate and Bluestem's ~94.1% (accept 93.8-94.4), and the healthcare initiative targets service/fill-rate investment ahead of the spring 2027 rebid rather than price concessions.
score_0_criteria: The loss attributed to price; or the fill-rate figures absent; or a healthcare win-back initiative built on discounting; or the rebid timing ignored in an initiative that claims the Heartland volume.
specific_file_locations: gpo_postmortem.eml (Enloe): 'Your pricing was within 1.5% of the awarded distributor. The award decision was driven by service commitments: the awarded distributor guaranteed a 98.5% fill rate and twice-weekly delivery to our rural facilities.' + '$14.2M in annual distributed volume'; ops_constraints_memo.md: healthcare fill rate 94.1%, $1.4M fix; VP memo: 'lost ... on price, plain and simple'.

title: Red-herring initiatives absent: no ghost-kitchen, Ozark, or Prairie Star plays
check_description: The portfolio does not build initiatives on the planted distractors: the ghost-kitchen opportunity (local TAM ~$6M per the market report's own appendix), the Ozark Produce acquisition teaser (out of scope per the CEO letter and CFO constraints), or a defensive land-grab against the Prairie Star DC rumor (single-sourced and debunked by the competitor brief). Analyzing or rejecting them in prose is fine; an initiative named for them is trap adoption.
score_1_criteria: The portfolio has at least one initiative, and no initiative name references ghost/virtual/delivery-only kitchens, Ozark Produce, or Prairie Star. Prose may discuss and dismiss them.
score_0_criteria: Any initiative is named as a ghost-kitchen, Ozark-acquisition, or Prairie Star-response play.
specific_file_locations: ghost_kitchen_market_report.md appendix: local addressable TAM ~$6M. acquisition_teaser_ozark_produce.eml vs ceo_engagement_letter.md scope. email_competitor_rumor.eml: single-source Prairie Star DC rumor; the competitor brief debunks.
v1_change: E5-D08/E5-D09: non-vacuity gate; synonyms for the ghost-kitchen play added ('virtual kitchen', 'delivery-only kitchen', ...); the bare token 'ozark' (which also matched an Ozarks-region territory initiative) narrowed to the Ozark Produce acquisition.
